# src/ — implementation

## Purpose
All hub and bridge code lives here on the Rust standard library only. Zero external crates is a hard constraint: every capability (crypto, JSON, HTTP, MCP) is implemented in-tree and unit-tested.

## Ownership
- `sha256.rs`, `hmac.rs`, `rand.rs`, `util.rs` — crypto primitives + shared helpers. FIPS 180-4 / RFC 2104/4231 vectors are load-bearing; do not weaken or remove them. `rand.rs` is kernel-CSPRNG-only (fails closed); `util.rs` holds constant-time compare, hex, clamping, query parsing.
- `client.rs` — hand-rolled HTTP/1.1 client used by the bridge and `wtf status`/`dashboard-url`; 30 s default timeouts.
- `lib.rs` — module registry; every module is `pub` for integration testing.
- `keccak.rs` — FIPS 202 SHA3-256/512 + SHAKE128/256 (sponge over Keccak-f[1600]); FIPS 202 KATs load-bearing.
- `aes.rs` — FIPS 197 AES-256 block cipher; Appendix C.3 + SP 800-38A vectors load-bearing.
- `gcm.rs` — AES-256-GCM (SP 800-38D): CTR keystream + GHASH; tag compare constant-time; McGrew-Viega appendix-B vectors load-bearing. 96-bit nonces only, never reuse key+nonce.
- `ntt_tables.rs` — Kyber NTT twiddle tables verbatim (Montgomery form, signed); do not regenerate by hand — source is pq-crystals kyber ref/ntt.c.
- `mlkem768.rs` — FIPS 203 ML-KEM-768: keygen/encaps/decaps. Key invariants: SampleNTT = raw rejection samples (no post-NTT); ntt consumes ZETAS[1..] ascending, intt consumes ZETAS[127..1] descending with f = 1441 = mont²/128; basemul gammas = ZETAS[64±i]; keygen applies poly_tomont (f = 2³² mod q) after accumulation; encaps returns K = G(m‖H(ek))[0..32] directly (no KDF). Official NIST ACVP KATs in `tests/vectors/` are load-bearing (keygen/encaps/decaps byte-exact). Cross-validated against pyca/cryptography (OpenSSL) and kyber-py.
- `sessions.rs` — hub-side encrypted session channel registry: members, ML-KEM-768 sealed key packages, seq-numbered ciphertext ring per session; hub stores ciphertext only and can read nothing. Fail-closed caps (sessions, members, msgs).
- `identity.rs` — bridge-side ML-KEM-768 identity keypair in `$WTF_HOME/identity.json` (0600), auto-generated on first use, corrupt file fails closed.
- `session_crypto.rs` — client-side sealing: ML-KEM-768 encapsulate of the 256-bit session key per member (AES-256-GCM wrap under SHA3-256(shared)), per-(session, sender) subkeys, AAD binds (session, sender, seq), deterministic 96-bit nonces from subkey+seq.
- `comms.rs` — COMMS ledger envelopes over session channels (bridge side): `wtf-comms-v1` JSON {event, scope, note, ts}; ledger vocabulary (checkin/update/intent-merge/checkout/blocked/announce/handoff); fail-closed validation (unknown events, empty/oversize notes); ledger-line rendering. The only agent surface sanctioned for secrets.
- `tasks.rs` — federated task dispatch (v0.18.0): durable cross-machine work records in `$WTF_HOME/tasks.json` (0600, atomic, replayed on boot). `Task {id, title, detail, repo, target, origin_device, origin_agent, assignee, session, state, result, error, attempts, created_at, updated_at, claimed_at, finished_at, lease_until}` with `STATES = queued|claimed|running|done|failed|blocked|cancelled` and `TERMINAL = done|failed|cancelled`. `target_matches` resolves `any`/bare machine name/`tier:<heavy|standard|edge>`/`arch:<os>-<arch>`; `valid_target` accepts exactly those shapes and fails closed on an unknown prefix, so a typo cannot degrade into match-everything. `can_transition` is the explicit legal-transition table — an out-of-order report fails closed rather than overwriting newer state. Claims carry `CLAIM_TTL_SECS` (900) leases; `expire_leases` re-queues an abandoned `claimed`/`running` task on read so a crashed peer cannot strand work. Ownership is enforced in the store: only the claiming device may start/finish/block, only the dispatching device may cancel. `to_state_json` feeds the dashboard TASKS card and `wtf tasks`. Pull-based by design — wtf never spawns a harness or an ssh session on another machine.
- `runner.rs` — agent runners (v0.19.0): decides *with what* a claimed task executes. `probe()` reports Orca (`which` tries orca-ide, orca-dev, orca) and Herdr availability with reasons; `choose(want, remote)` resolves `auto` by preference order (Orca first) or honors an explicit name exactly, failing closed when absent rather than downgrading. `argv`/`argv_with_agent` build the command line as an array — never a shell — and are unit-tested because the flag shape is the contract: Orca gets `orchestration worker-start --spec <s> --agent <id> [--on <env> --worktree new-top-level | --worktree path:<dir>] --json` (remote is addressed by a PAIRED environment, never a hostname); Herdr gets `[--machine <label>] agent start --prompt <s> --json`. `DEFAULT_ORCA_AGENT = "codex"` because `worker-start` refuses to create a terminal without `--agent`. `start_with_agent` runs it under a wall-clock cap (`run_with_timeout`, killed on expiry) and extracts the handle from the runner's JSON envelope, degrading to no handle rather than failing a launch that already happened. `which` rejects path-like names so a peer cannot name a binary.
- Session pairing keys + repo tags (v0.12.0): `sessions.rs` stores `pairing_hash` (SHA-256 of the 256-bit pairing key; key itself never on the hub) + `repo` per session; `create` returns the key once; `check_pairing` constant-time; `join_or_refresh` admits pairing joiners and refreshes ek on identity rotation; join route accepts `pairing` (wrong key = uniform 403). MCP: `session_create` takes `repo` and surfaces the pairing key; `session_join` takes `pairing`; `auto_seal_members` (before send/read) seals the key to any member lacking a package; `session_read` recovers the key from seals; `session_list` shows repo; `wtf sessions` CLI lists chats + local pairing keys (creator machine).
- `federation.rs` — hub federation identity + peer table (`federation.json` 0600: this hub's `name`, per-peer `{name, url, device, device_key}` where `device_key` is the credential THE PEER issued, name `fed-<hub-name>`), the dashboard capability token (`dashboard_capability` 0600, 64-hex, auto-minted, rotate = delete + restart), and push-envelope shape validation (fail-closed, ≤500 events).
- `replicate.rs` — outbound replication: per-peer loop pushing locally-originated events (`events_since(origin=this-hub, cursor)`) and an anti-entropy sweep (pull the peer's own events; self-pull verifies the link) every 10 s, over the standard HMAC device lane (`auth.rs` untouched). Warns throttle to one event per 5 min per peer; failures never crash the hub.
- `json.rs` — strict depth-limited parser + serializer; the only JSON path for config, wire, and storage.
- `http.rs`, `client.rs` — hand-rolled HTTP/1.1. Server enforces 32 KiB head / 1 MiB body / 100 headers / 15 s timeouts; `Transfer-Encoding` requests get `501` by design.
- `auth.rs` — HMAC-SHA256 request signing (standard-crypto transport lane). Canonical string: `wtf-hmac-v1
METHOD
path-and-query
ts
nonce
sha256hex(body)`. ±300 s skew; per-device nonce replay cache. Device lookup happens before nonce consumption so callers can reload the keystore and retry.
- `config.rs` — `$WTF_HOME` layout (default `~/.config/wtf-mcp`), atomic writes, `0600` key files, KeyStore issue/revoke/rotate, BridgeConfig with env overrides `WTF_HUB_URL` / `WTF_DEVICE_NAME` / `WTF_DEVICE_KEY`. HubConfig carries an optional `advertised_url` (set via `wtf url`) that wins over LAN auto-detection in `lan_url()`, plus `enroll_secret` (256-bit hex): auto-generated on first serve, backfilled into pre-0.9 configs on load (best-effort persist), all fields written through the single `save_at` (0600, atomic), and `rotate_enroll_secret[_at]` mints a fresh secret instantly, invalidating outstanding copies. `BridgeConfig::validate` accepts `http://` and `https://`. `enroll_tokens.json` (0600) is the EnrollTokenStore: records carry name + SHA-256(token) + expiry + `used`; `issue` supersedes prior same-name records, ttl 1..=86400 s (default 600); `consume` burns on success only; persist is atomic 0600 and its failure rolls the in-memory burn back (`TokenError::Store`).
- `chat.rs` — router chat (v0.16.0, replaces the stripped `executor.rs`): PASSIVE probe of the operator-run local-router (`router_alive()`, `router_state_json()`, `router_models()` — read-only GETs, 2 s cache, never spawn/stop/restart local-router/fcc-server/fcc-dsh), model discovery (`preferred_model()`: llama.cpp qwen3 abliterated → qwen3 → llama.cpp → `local-router/fallback-models`), and OpenAI completions (`chat_completion()` → `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1/chat/completions`, pure `chat_request_body()`/`chat_parse_reply()` helpers, 180 s IO timeout, fails closed when :11434 is down). All agent-harness logic deleted (catalog, tmux dispatch, term sessions).
- `fed_shell.rs` — federated multi-machine shell engine (v0.15.2+): virtual `~/` cluster root representing connected machines (`~/mac`, `~/windows`, etc.); discovery of local node, peers, and SSH hosts; persistent per-architecture Last Known Good Location (LKGL) tracking via `$WTF_HOME/lkgl.json`; compute tier classification (`heavy`, `standard`, `edge`); synchronized federated OMP configuration (`$WTF_HOME/fed_omp_config.json`); and cross-architecture compound command execution in a single prompt. AST verified via GitNexus: `exec_federated` executes commands in isolated subpaths or machine LKGLs, injecting loopback proxy environment `OLLAMA_HOST=127.0.0.1:11434` and `LOCAL_ROUTER_URL=http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1`.
- `store.rs` — `events.jsonl` is the source of truth (replayed on start, rotates at 10 MB); 1000 events in memory; generation counter drives SSE pushes. Events carry `origin` (originating hub's fed name; "" = pre-federation), `origin_id` (monotonic AT the origin), and `repo` (project label). Locally-recorded events stamp this hub's name (`Store::set_origin_name`, wired at serve); `ingest` dedupes on (origin, origin_id), assigns local ids, and applies last-writer-wins on agent cards by ts; cursors via `max_origin_id`/`events_since`. Two providers are injected at serve time for the state payload: `set_sessions_provider` (session summaries) and `set_tasks_provider` (the federated task board from `tasks::TaskStore::to_state_json`); both default to empty so pre-wiring callers stay correct.
- `identities.json` (0600) — Hub identity registry (`Hub.identities`): device -> ML-KEM-768 ek registrations persist to `$WTF_HOME/identities.json` (0600, atomic write via `config.rs::save_at`) on registration and session join, and rehydrate on hub startup from disk and active session members (`load_persisted_identities` / `persist_identities`). Auto-seals flow across restarts without re-joining.
- `api.rs` — route table + authz: `/healthz` open; the dashboard page at `/w/<capability>` (singular capability URL valid across loopback, LAN, and remote); `/stream` and `/api/v1/state` accept capability (`?cap=`, header, or bearer) or device auth; `checkin`/`event`/`heartbeat`/`identity` device-only (checkin/event accept an optional `repo`); `/api/v1/devices` and session GET/list accept capability or device; `/api/v1/chat/completions` (POST) is a thin authenticated proxy to the operator-run router (fails closed 502 when :11434 is down); `/api/v1/shell/machines`, `/api/v1/shell/config`, and `/api/v1/shell/exec` are operator capability gated; `/api/v1/router/status` (GET) is a PASSIVE read-only probe of the operator-run local-router (:11434) — `/api/v1/router/restart` was removed (uniform 404; hub never spawns/stops router infra); the v0.15 `/api/v1/term/*` executor-terminal and `/api/v1/agents/available` routes were removed (uniform 404) in v0.16.0, and the `/api/v1/bins*` routes were removed in v0.17.0 (also uniform 404); session `seal`/`seals`/`send`/`recv` are device-only and member-gated; `POST /api/v1/enroll` is token/psk-gated as before; `POST /api/v1/fed/push` + `GET /api/v1/fed/pull?origin=&after=` are gated on a `fed-*` device credential, `GET /api/v1/fed/peers` is device auth. Task dispatch (v0.18.0): `GET /api/v1/tasks` and `GET /api/v1/tasks/board` are the board (capability or device); `POST /api/v1/tasks` dispatches (device only, record stamped with the dispatching device); `POST /api/v1/tasks/claim` takes the oldest queued task this machine can serve and answers `{ok, task: record|null}` in both cases (device only); `GET /api/v1/tasks/{id}` reads one record; `POST /api/v1/tasks/{id}/{start,finish,block,bind,cancel}` mutate it (device only; start/finish/block require the claiming device, cancel requires the dispatching device). Every dashboard-path failure is the same uniform 404 as unknown routes (no auth oracle; R5 legacy `?k=` retired). The keystore reloads from disk on every authenticated request; revoked devices fail closed (401). State JSON agents carry `repo` + `origin`, and the payload carries the `tasks` board. Agent runners (v0.19.0): `GET /api/v1/tasks/runners` is a read-only probe (capability or device) answering which of orca/herdr can start work here and which `auto` would pick; `POST /api/v1/tasks/{id}/run` (device only, claiming device only) resolves the runner, launches the agent under a wall-clock cap, records the handle, and moves the task to `running` — it is the one route that starts an external runtime. `task_run` deliberately receives the already-authenticated device instead of re-running `device_auth`, which would consume the request nonce twice and trip the replay guard.
- `dashboard.rs` — embedded single-page dark UI; no external assets; EventSource live updates. Integrates top-level Studio: User Chat & SWE-bench Agent Orchestration Studio paired side-by-side with the Federated Multi-Machine Shell (`~/` virtual root with machine quick-jumps, architecture LKGL context, compute tiers, and cross-architecture multi-prompt execution). Studio chat pane POSTs `/api/v1/chat/completions` and renders the reply with its model (lane viewer is read-only from the dashboard). Passive local-router status badge in header (read-only probe; no restart button, no auto-reconnect — the router is operator-run infrastructure). Agents group by origin hub with origin chips; each agent/event shows its repo chip. SESSIONS card and the v0.18.0 TASKS card — the paste-bin grid and its scope switcher were removed in v0.17.0. TASKS renders the federated board: per-state count pills, then one row per work item with state pill, title, repo, target → assignee, bound chat, attempt count, and the result/error body (failed rows in `--err`); detail is collapsed behind a toggle so the board stays scannable.
- `mcp.rs` — stdio JSON-RPC 2.0 bridge (`initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `ping`); twenty-four tools (`check_in`, `log_event`, `wtf_is_going_on`, `ping`, `hub_info`, `env_report`, `env_probe`, `session_create`, `session_list`, `session_join`, `session_seal`, `session_send`, `session_read`, `comms_post`, `comms_read`, `task_dispatch`, `task_claim`, `task_report`, `task_status`, `task_run`, `runner_probe`, `chat`, `router_status`); application failures are `isError:true` results, never protocol errors; 60 s heartbeat thread; shared text formatter also used by `wtf status`; `instructions` + tool descriptions mandate chain-of-draft reporting (terse fragments, <=5 words) and carry the cross-machine WORK rule — delegate to another machine with `task_dispatch`, never over ad-hoc ssh or by driving a remote agent session; `hub_info` answers the operator's where-is-the-hub question without ever exposing the capability token over MCP. `decode` accepts every 2xx (a created task answers 201) and surfaces the hub's own `error` text on failure so an agent can act on the reason. Paste-bin tools (`read_bin`/`write_bin`/`list_bins`) were removed in v0.17.0.
- `main.rs` — CLI: `serve` (mints the hub fed name on first run, stamps it as event origin, spawns replicator when peers exist, prints singular capability URL `http://<host>:<port>/w/<capability>`), `key issue|list|revoke`, `url` (get/set/clear advertised URL), `setup`, `join`, `agent`, `status`, `dashboard-url` (prints canonical loopback capability URL and LAN capability link), `tasks` (v0.18.0: review the federated task board from any machine, capability-gated, `--state` filter), `enroll-token` (ephemeral one-time token; burns on handshake), `enroll` (redeem token or PSK), `enroll-secret` (display or `--rotate` PSK), `skill install|print` (distributes `.agents/skills/wtf-is-going-on-mcp/SKILL.md`), `federate add|list|remove`, `help`. `resolve_hub_and_cap` is the shared hub-URL/capability resolver used by the operator read commands.

## Local Contracts
- No third-party dependencies in `Cargo.toml`, ever. Implement or do without.
- **Hard-code everything; own your dependencies** (operator directive 2026-09-01): new capabilities (protocols, codecs, anything) get implemented in this tree with unit tests + official vectors — never vendored from crates.io.
- No literal IP addresses in source or docs authored by agents (tooling redacts them); build addresses from constants at runtime, use `localhost` in examples.
- Secrets (device keys, capability token) go only into `0600` files under `$WTF_HOME` or the one-time `wtf key issue` output; never commit or log them.
- Standard crypto for transport only. PQC (FIPS 203/204/205) is mandatory for secrets at rest and in transit.
- Bridge URLs are `http://` (trusted LAN or encrypted overlay) or `https://` (TLS-terminating proxy). The HMAC signature is the authenticity root in every topology; TLS is never implemented in-tree.
- Fail closed: unparseable input is a 4xx, auth errors never reveal which factor failed.

## Work Guidance
- Keep the HTTP parser strict; raise limits deliberately, never silently.
- A new endpoint must land in three places together: `api.rs` dispatch, the `known_path` list, and the authz model comment at the top of `api.rs`. A route under a `/api/v1/<thing>/` prefix must also be exempted from the `{id}` fallthrough in that resource's path parser (see `task_path`), or `POST /api/v1/tasks/claim` is read as task id `claim`.
- A new resource returns ONE wire shape for a given route. A success body that changes shape on the empty case forces every caller to branch, and a mis-branch reports "nothing found" while the mutation already happened.
- Task dispatch stays pull-based: never add a hub-side spawn, an ssh exec, or a remote-harness launch to satisfy a queued task. Wire queued state is a legitimate resting state. The ONE exception is `POST /tasks/{id}/run`, which starts a runtime for a task a device has already claimed — it never runs speculatively, and it never picks the target.
- A handler runs `device_auth` exactly once per request: the nonce is consumed on verification, so a second call in the same request fails as a replay (401). Thread the verified device into helpers instead of re-authenticating.
- A route that starts an external process needs a read timeout sized for it — the client default (10 s) reports a timeout while the work has in fact started. `api_post_with_timeout` exists for this.
- Runner argv is a contract with another team's CLI: build it as a Vec, unit-test the exact flags, and pass specs as single argv words. Adding a runtime means adding a `RUNNERS` entry, an `argv` arm, a probe arm, and a test — never a `sh -c`.
- Federation contract: every event needs `origin` + `origin_id` before it may cross the wire; `ingest` dedupe is the loop-breaker — never bypass it. Peer URLs must be stable across hub restarts; `federate add` adopts the peer's REAL fed name (label is cosmetic).
- Dashboard paths: `/w/<capability>` is the only page route; any change to dashboard gating must keep the uniform-404 property (wrong token == unknown path).
- Bridge tools report failures as tool results, keeping the JSON-RPC layer for protocol faults only.

## Verification
- `cargo test` — 132 unit tests + 14 e2e tests green.
- `cargo build --release` must succeed (lto, codegen-units=1, panic=abort, overflow-checks).
- rustfmt/clippy are not installed in this environment; run `cargo fmt`/`cargo clippy -- -D warnings` when available.
